reasons: Scale (rule 4) against the stated mini croissant (~60mm): the huggies are drawn about half a croissant long, about +45% (about 26mm against 18mm). The upright huggie is ~330px across (x 1055-1385, y 1175-1521), leaning on the middle croissant with its base on the paper. The flat huggie is ~313px (x 349-662, y 1300-1475). The middle croissant runs ~680px tip to end (x 724-1402, ~690px chord) and the left croissant ~635px (x 141-773). That gives a raw ratio of 0.48-0.49 against a true 0.30 (18/60), i.e. +60%. The hoops sit 60-180px lower in the frame than the croissant centres. The two identical hoops differ 5% in width over an 84px floor offset, so allowing 8-14% for nearness gives +40-47%. Reading the croissants as turned into depth (their two ends meet the paper 70-135px apart in height, with the camera ~15 deg above the paper) lowers that. The left croissant, which lies almost side-on, still gives +31% (the middle one could give as little as +12%). On screen the hoops read as half a croissant long. Nothing marks the croissants as minis, so a shopper reads full-size bakery croissants and hoops of about 45-50mm, not 18mm huggies. The prompt asked for a quarter of a croissant (0.25); the plate drew ~0.47 (~1.9x).
notes: Construction matches listing-1/listing-5. Chunky mirror-polished yellow gold, the whole outer surface in deep smooth diagonal twist ridges (not a wire braid, not plain), a smooth inner wall, no stones. The upright hoop's thin hinge post is seated across the top into the ridged end (closed); the flat hoop shows the post at the back-left, as in listing-5. Minor: the upright hoop's tube reads a little slimmer than listing-1 (opening ~0.6 of the outer width against ~0.5).
Exactly the pair and nothing else. Three croissants (the third is cut by the right edge) and pastry flakes only; no plate, butter, jam or hands. No text anywhere.
Physics is fine. The upright hoop leans on the croissant with its foot on the paper and a shadow; the flat hoop lies on its side with a dark contact line.

Palette: the lit paper is peach (~RGB 244,205,170, hue 28). The shadowed wall that fills the top ~40% is a muted mocha-rose (~RGB 172,134,111, hue 22, sat 0.33). That is acceptable as warm shadow, but it is on the taupe side of dusty rose. Hard low sun from the left with crisp long shadows and a diagonal light band, as asked.
An 8-point starburst on the flat hoop (~(600,1310)) looks like a filter; minor.
At true scale this would be a strong ad (~8.7). The twist/croissant rhyme reads instantly, the gold is the brightest thing in frame, and the top 40% is calm headline space.
fix: Same scene, light and build; shrink the huggies and make the croissants read as minis. Ask for each huggie at about one fifth of a croissant's length, a ratio of ~0.19: the true ratio is 0.30, divided by the generator's ~1.6x. This plate drew ~0.47 from a requested 0.25, ~1.9x. Wording: 'each mini croissant is five huggies long; the two huggies side by side span less than half a croissant'. Ask for small, tightly rolled mini croissants with only 4-5 turns. Lay them side-on in one line across the frame, with the huggies in the row at the same depth, not in front of it. Bring the camera close enough that the row spans the frame width, so the hoops stay big in frame at true size. Keep the tube chunky (opening about half the outer width), the ridges and the seated hinge exactly. Warm the shadowed wall from mocha toward dusty rose.

reasons: Scale (rule 4) against the tall lemonade glass (~70mm wide): the earring is drawn about twice its true size, about +105%. The glass is ~645px across at the rim (outer edges x 603 and 1248), ~9.2px/mm. The earring hangs on the glass's right silhouette edge, at the same depth as that width, so no depth correction applies. The earring runs from the top of the C and the post (y ~418) to the heart's point (y ~930): ~512px, ~56mm against 27mm. The C alone is ~347px (y 418-765), ~38mm against ~17mm (+120%). The heart is ~130px wide (x 1070-1200, y 792-932), ~14mm against 9mm (+55%). Earring length to glass width is 0.79 against a true 0.39. The prompt asked for 0.33 ('as wide as three earrings are long'), so the generator drew ~2.4x the request, stretching the C most.
notes: Construction matches listing-1/listing-5. It is a tall, narrow white-metal C, about 2.7 hearts tall and 1.3 hearts wide (listing ~2.4 x 1.2), opening toward the glass. About 13-15 round brilliants sit in claws along the outer front edge, with upright baguettes along the inner wall. The plain back of the hoop shows as in listing-5, and a straight post projects from the top. One pale aqua heart in a claw basket hangs point-down from the bottom tip on a small loop. One earring only; no straw, fruit slice, other jewellery or text.

At zoom (1020-1290, 390-800) the outer brilliants read smoky grey-brown because they mirror the terracotta wall. At phone size the C still reads silver and sparkly, but the reshoot should keep them clear white.
Physics is plausible. The post lies over the rim into the glass, the C hangs against the outer wall, and the heart hangs free among the condensation beads.

Palette: peach paper (~RGB 251,209,179, hue 25) under a deep terracotta-rose wall that fills the top ~45% (~RGB 152,96,79, hue 14, sat 0.48, value 0.6). The wall gives calm copy space top left but is heavier than blush. Hard sun with a crisp diagonal shadow, as asked.

The 'one more icy drop' idea reads in about a second. Drawn at true size in this framing, the earring would be half as tall and small in frame, so the reshoot needs a closer camera, not a bigger earring.
fix: Keep the scene and the build; shrink the earring and move the camera closer. Ask for the whole earring at about a quarter of the glass's width, a ratio of ~0.24: the true ratio is 0.39, divided by ~1.6. Wording: 'the glass is four earrings wide; the C is about one seventh of the glass's width and the heart about one twelfth'. This plate drew ~2.4x its request, stretching the C most. If the C still comes out long, step down to 'the glass is five earrings wide'. Frame only the top third of the glass, with the rim spanning ~60% of the frame width, so the earring stays prominent at true size. Keep the C hooked over the rim (post inside, C outside) and the heart hanging among the beads. Ask for the outer brilliants to stay bright clear white. Lift the wall from terracotta toward dusty rose.

reasons: Scale (rule 4): the earring is about +40% oversized against the shuttlecock (disc ~19-21mm against 14mm; range +30% to +50%). The shuttlecock lies on its side with the cork base (the hard referent) cut off by the right edge, so scale comes from the feather skirt. The disc is ~406px across (x 718-1124, y 842-1261), the drop pearl ~240px (x 805-1045, y 1349-1599), and the earring ~757px long. The skirt's tip circle spans ~1300px top to bottom: feather tips from y ~321 down to the lowest feathers at y ~1620. A feather shuttlecock's tip circle is 58-68mm, so the scale is ~20-21px/mm. That gives a disc of ~19-20mm and an earring of ~36mm against 26mm. Second check: the cut feather tips step ~220-250px apart, ~12.4mm per feather on a 16-feather, ~63mm skirt (~19px/mm). By that measure the disc spans ~1.7 feather widths, where the prompt asked for about one. Taking off ~5% because the earring sits just in front of the feathers leaves +30-50%. The drop pearl alone is ~+15%. The prompt asked for 3.5 earrings to a shuttlecock's height (0.29); the plate shows ~0.52 of the inferred 70mm height (~1.8x).
notes: Product matches listing-1/listing-5. Warm yellow gold; a polished rim around a sunburst of ~20-22 slim clear baguettes set as rays with bead claws; a beaded collar around the centre pearl; one larger white drop pearl on a short gold bail with a cap. Exactly two pearls. Pearl-to-disc ratio ~0.59 (listing-5 ~0.61). One earring; no loose pearls, racket, net or text.

The attachment is not shown. The prompt's 'hooked at the feather's edge' did not happen: the disc sits in front of the skirt's left edge. The nearest visible feather edge runs at x ~950-1000 above and below the disc, just right of the post (~(920,1050)). The feathers behind the rim are slightly out of focus, and there is no contact shadow. It could only be pinned through a hidden feather. I did not judge it impossible, but it reads as hovering, so the reshoot should show the hold.

The shuttlecock lies on its side, showing only feathers and the thread binding, instead of standing on its cork. It still reads as a shuttlecock, but more slowly, and the referent the brief names is missing.

Light comes from the right (the feathered shadow falls left), not from the left as asked; that is acceptable. Large dark cocoa areas make the frame heavier than blush and ivory: the top band is ~RGB 115,76,60 (value 0.45) and the floor shadow ~RGB 109,67,48. The lit paper is peach (~RGB 240,194,166, hue 23).
The baguette sunburst rhymes beautifully with the radiating feathers and shafts. At true size, hung visibly from a feather of an upright shuttlecock, this could be a strong 'Smash.' frame.
fix: Show the whole shuttlecock standing upright on its cork base (cork ~25mm, ~70mm tall) and shrink the earring. Ask for it at about 0.23 of the shuttlecock's height, the true 0.37 divided by ~1.6: 'the shuttlecock is four and a half earrings tall'. Ask for the disc at about a third of the cork base's width, the true 0.56 divided by ~1.6. This plate drew ~1.8x its request. Show the hold: the stud's post pushed through the vane of one feather near its tip, the disc lying flat against that feather with a small contact shadow, and the pearl drop hanging free and plumb below the skirt's edge. Keep the sunburst, beaded collar and two-pearl build exactly. Frame close, with the shuttlecock ~60% of the frame height. Lift the cocoa wall and shadows toward dusty rose.

One huggie only, and every other cell holds clear ice. No drink, hands, loose pearls or other jewellery. No text or embossing on the tray, paper or ice.

Physics: the hoop lies flat and dry on the cell floor with a dark contact line along its lower edges. Its shadow and the lit oval of floor seen through its opening agree with the light from the upper left.
Palette: blush-peach silicone (~RGB 246,210,182, hue 26) on peach paper (~RGB 247,216,189, hue 28), with warm shadows and clear ice. It is on the peach side of blush, but not beige, sand or tan.

As an ad: 'Cool, squared.' reads in under a second, with one gold square where an ice cube should be, the only warm metal in a cool grid. The gold is the sharpest, brightest thing in frame. The ice is convincing (cloudy cores, melt beads, wet dividers), and the hard light gives crisp speculars. Two starburst flares on the gold (~(750,1185) and ~(1050,1110)) look like a filter. The hoop is only ~18% of the frame width.
The PNG carries an alpha channel (fully opaque); flatten it to RGB before upload.
fix: Runs as-is. Optional polish for a reshoot: keep the 0.4 scale request, which landed at about +20%. Leave the top third calmer (fewer, emptier cells, or tilt the tray so blank peach paper shows top left) for the headline. Replace the two starbursts with a single hard specular.
